name: Bump-on-tail instability
description: A minority “bump” of fast particles on the tail of an otherwise Maxwellian distribution drives Langmuir waves unstable, feeding energy into the field until particle trapping saturates it.

name: Diocotron instability
description: A sheared E×B ring of charge is unstable: a tiny azimuthal perturbation grows, rippling the ring's edges — the onset of a rotating pattern of vortices.

name: ITG drift wave
description: A magnetized plasma column with radial density and temperature gradients drives a helical drift wave unstable — the basic mechanism behind ion-temperature-gradient (ITG) turbulence.

name: Maxwell light-wave dispersion
description: Excite a broadband electric field and recover the vacuum dispersion relation ω = ck with Struphy’s FEEC Maxwell solver.

name: Poisson time-dependent source
description: Drive a 1D Poisson solve with an oscillating cosine-mode charge density and compare Struphy’s FEEC potential against the exact solution, at every time step.

name: Strong Landau damping
description: A large-amplitude perturbation drives a Vlasov-Ampère plasma into the nonlinear regime — particles trap in the field's potential wells, and the field energy bounces instead of decaying smoothly.

name: Two-stream instability
description: Two counter-streaming Maxwellian beams are kinetically unstable — a tiny perturbation grows exponentially, drawing energy from the beams, until particle trapping saturates the growth.

name: Vlasov particle orbits in a tokamak
description: Trace full-orbit test particles through a tokamak’s magnetic field and watch them gyrate around field lines while circulating -- or bouncing -- through the torus.

name: Weak Landau damping
description: A tiny electrostatic perturbation phase-mixes away in a collisionless plasma — the classic Landau-damping benchmark, compared here against its analytically known damping rate.

name: Weibel instability
description: A temperature-anisotropic plasma spontaneously generates a magnetic field: a tiny seed perturbation grows exponentially, tapping the excess perpendicular thermal energy.
